criteria.question: does the flycns simulator, set to Shiu et al. 2024's choices, reproduce their model's outputs on their own FlyWire v630 data (A1); and does the male CNS drive MN9 under the same choices (M1)?
does Shiu et al. 2024's own code, on its own released data and in its own package versions, reproduce its released sugar -> MN9 output when run here?

protocol.stimulus: the 21 sugar GRNs of figures.ipynb (first neu_sugar list) at 100 Hz (their r_poi)
protocol.code: their run_exp, unmodified, n_proc = all cores
protocol.readout: spikes per trial of MN9 720575940660219265 (contralateral) and 720575940645521262

A0_S1_mn9_contra_magnitude.rule: the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval (flycns.stats.bootstrap_diff, seed 0) of our contralateral MN9 mean minus the published 30 trials' mean lies within +/-6.7 Hz: PASS; wholly outside: FAIL; else UNRESOLVED

A0_S2_mn9_reliability.rule: contralateral MN9 fires in at least 29 of 30 trials (a count, no interval)

A0_S3_laterality.rule: BOTH parts: contralateral minus ipsilateral per trial, 95% bootstrap interval above 0; our ipsilateral mean minus the published one, 95% bootstrap interval within +/-4.86 Hz

criteria.decision: A0 passes only if all three checks PASS; then phase 1 continues with A1 and M1 after review

preregistered_phase1.data: FlyWire v630 from the pinned reference repository (PINS); sugar, bitter and MN9 ids from its figures.ipynb; the per-neuron sign is the repository's Excitatory column (Shiu's rule: GABA and glutamate inhibitory; acetylcholine and the amines excitatory), mapped onto graph.SIGN_MAP labels

a1_settings.reset: v and g reset at a spike; g frozen while refractory
a1_settings.stimulation: stimulated cells stay in the network; Poisson input of 250 x w_syn per event, refractory 0

checks.S1_sugar_mn9_magnitude: sugar GRNs (21 ids) at 100 Hz, 30 trials: the 95% bootstrap interval of (our contralateral MN9 mean - the published 30 trials' mean) lies within +/-6.7 Hz
checks.S2_reliability: contralateral MN9 fires (>= 1 spike) in at least 29 of 30 trials
checks.S3_laterality: BOTH: contralateral minus ipsilateral (paired per trial) above 0, AND ipsilateral within +/-4.86 Hz of the published 48.63 Hz (two samples)
checks.S4_calibration_reproduced: MN9 at 100 Hz divided by the maximum of the MN9 means at 50, 100, 150 and 200 Hz (30 trials each), 95% bootstrap interval within [0.7, 0.9] (the paper: W_syn chosen so that 100 Hz gives 'roughly 80% of maximal MN9 firing')
checks.S5_bitter_suppression: sugar GRNs at 100 Hz plus bitter GRNs (21 ids, figures.ipynb) at 0, 50, 100, 150 and 200 Hz, 30 trials each. PASS if BOTH: the 95% bootstrap interval of MN9(sugar 100 + bitter 100) - MN9(sugar 100 + bitter 0) lies below 0, AND the 95% bootstrap interval of the Spearman rank correlation between bitter rate and per-trial contralateral MN9 rate (150 trials) lies below 0. FAIL if either interval lies wholly at or above 0; UNRESOLVED otherwise. Qualitative, from the paper's text. If the authors' archived Fig 3a values become available, a quantitative S5b is registered separately before it is scored; S5 is never changed
checks.S6_wiring_control: 100 weight shuffles keeping the global weight distribution (as the paper), 1 trial each, sugar at 100 Hz. A shuffle 'activates MN9' if its contralateral MN9 rate reaches T = 51.4 Hz. Derivation: T is the 1st percentile of a normal fit to the 30 released real-wiring trials (mean 67.03, SD 6.71 Hz; their minimum is 53 Hz), i.e. a rate the real wiring reaches in 99% of trials. PASS if at most 5 of 100 shuffles activate MN9 (the paper: 1 of 100; if the true probability were 1%, 6 or more of 100 would occur with probability below 0.001); FAIL otherwise
checks.M1_male_mn9: MaleCNS under the A1 settings, the sugar set and MN9 readout of flycns check F3 (LB3b and LB3c at 100 Hz), 30 trials: MN9 'responds' if the 95% bootstrap interval of its rate lies above 0.5 Hz (the F3 band)

preregistered_phase1.ladder: L1-L6, reported and not scored: from A1, one setting switched to its flycns value at a time (reset, stimulation, connection floor 5, w_scale 0.4, motor adaptation), then all together
preregistered_phase1.decision_rule: A0 fails: the reference does not reproduce here; stop. A0 passes and A1 fails: flycns differs beyond the listed settings; bisect first. A1 passes and M1 responds: the male MN9 zero is caused by flycns settings (the ladder names which). A1 passes and M1 does not respond: the male zero is wiring or annotation, not the simulator

a1_integration.value: exact (Brian2 method 'linear', as Shiu et al.'s model.py)
a1_integration.why: the approved phase-1 plan lists it as A1 setting 8; the registered a1_settings omitted it; found before any A1 code existed
a1_integration.ladder: Le: A1 with Euler integration (flycns's value), reported and not scored; L6 (all settings at their flycns values) includes Euler

m1_connection_floor.why: the MaleCNS data hold no connection below 5 synapses (scripts/fetch_malecns.py queries weight >= 5)
m1_connection_floor.other_settings: every other A1 setting, exact integration included
m1_connection_floor.reading: if M1 does not respond and L3 (A1 at floor 5) loses MN9, a MaleCNS fetch down to 1 synapse comes before any conclusion of 'wiring or annotation'

criteria.m1_unknown_transmitter: flycns's handling (outputs dropped); the count of such neurons is reported with M1

criteria.question: does flycns in Shiu-compatible settings reproduce the authors' published sugar dose curve?

reference.readout: MN9 720575940660219265, contralateral; spikes per 1-s trial, 30 trials

criteria.relation_to_S4: separate; S4 (pre-registered in results/shiu2024_a0/) is unchanged and scores UNRESOLVED on the authors' own Fig 1 output (0.705, 95% interval 0.686-0.724)

protocol.reuse: S4's runs (sugar 50, 100, 150 and 200 Hz); no new arms

S4b_dose_curve_matches_published.rule: at each of sugar 50, 100, 150 and 200 Hz, the 95% bootstrap interval (two samples of 30 trials) of our contralateral MN9 mean minus the published mean lies within +/-6.7 Hz: PASS if all 4 do; FAIL if any lies wholly outside; UNRESOLVED otherwise
S4b_dose_curve_matches_published.margin_derivation: S5b's: 10% of the published sugar-alone rate (67.0 Hz), as an absolute margin

criteria.question: does flycns in Shiu-compatible settings reproduce the authors' published bitter suppression curve?

reference.readout: MN9 720575940660219265, contralateral; spikes per 1-s trial, 30 trials

criteria.relation_to_S5: separate; S5 (qualitative, pre-registered in results/shiu2024_a0/) is unchanged

protocol.reuse: bitter 0, 100 and 200 Hz are S5's runs; 20, 40, 60, 80 and 120 Hz are new arms

S5b_bitter_curve_matches_published.rule: at each of the 8 bitter rates, the 95% bootstrap interval (two samples of 30 trials) of our contralateral MN9 mean minus the published mean lies within +/-6.7 Hz: PASS if all 8 do; FAIL if any lies wholly outside; UNRESOLVED otherwise
S5b_bitter_curve_matches_published.margin_derivation: 10% of the published sugar-alone rate (67.0 Hz), the S1 scale, as an absolute margin at every point

a1_settings.note: flycns.model.SimOptions(reset='v_and_g', stimulation='kick', integration='exact', adaptation=False); LIFParams(w_scale=1.0); every connection of the repository (floor 1); sign = its Excitatory column; electrical synapses off; peptides off

data.flywire: the repository's completeness table (every neuron, its root id) and connectivity table (pre, post, synapse count, Excitatory sign), verified against the sha256 of the A0 registration; sugar and bitter GRNs: the neu_sugar and neu_bitter lists of figures.ipynb; the two MN9s are labelled superclass cb_motor (they are the cells flycns's motor adaptation would act on; ladder L5); no other cell is labelled
data.malecns: data/ as pinned by data/MANIFEST.json, load_graph(min_weight=5, amines='excitatory'); sugar: every LB3b and LB3c cell; MN9: every cell of type MN9

implementation.trial: restore the stored initial state, set the Poisson rates (sugar GRNs, bitter GRNs), run 1000 ms; spikes counted per neuron; one network per arm, built once; seeds 1, 2, ... in arm order; the random stream runs on across trials (Brian2 restore keeps it)
implementation.shuffle: S6: per shuffle k (0-99), the signed per-connection weights of the recurrent network are permuted among the existing connections (numpy default_rng(10000 + k)), keeping the global weight distribution; one 1000 ms trial at sugar 100 Hz; contralateral MN9 rate

readouts.m1: mean spikes per MN9 cell per second, per trial

implementation.intervals: flycns.stats: percentile bootstrap, 2,000 resamples, seed 0; multi-arm statistics resample every arm on its own

published.s1_s3: results/example/sugarR_100Hz.parquet of the reference repository (as A0)

S2_reliability.rule: contralateral MN9 fires in >= 29 of 30 trials

S4_calibration_reproduced.note: the authors' own Fig 1 output also scores UNRESOLVED here (S4b)

S5_bitter_suppression.scored_as: suppression = MN9(sugar 100) - MN9(sugar 100 + bitter 100), and minus the Spearman rho of per-trial MN9 against bitter rate (150 trials): both intervals must lie above 0 (lower edge exclusive), i.e. the registered 'below 0'; FAIL if either lies wholly at or below it

S6_wiring_control.rule: at most 5 of 100 shuffles reach 51.4 Hz contralateral MN9

M1_male_mn9.scored_as: PASS = responds (interval above 0.5 Hz, lower edge exclusive); FAIL = does not

a1_definition.principle: reference-calibrated: a check counts towards A1 only if the reference model (Shiu et al.'s own code, or its released output) passes it under the same procedure. A check the reference itself cannot pass cannot tell the two simulators apart

reference.S1_S2_S3: A0 passed all three (reference run 1, results/shiu2024_a0/a0.json)
reference.S4: the reference's own Fig 1 output scores 0.705, 95% interval 0.686-0.724: UNRESOLVED, so S4 does not count; it is scored and reported
reference.S4b_S5b: the reference's released output is the comparison itself
reference.S5: the reference's released output passes on the rates it has (bitter 0, 100, 200 Hz; 50 and 150 Hz were not released): suppression 63.0 Hz (61.2 to 64.8), minus rho 0.946 (0.925 to 0.962)
reference.S6: no released shuffle output. If A1's S6 FAILs, the reference's own code runs the same 100 shuffles (scripts/shiu2024_run_shuffles.py: the same permutation of the same weight array, in file order, one 1 s trial each, sugar 100 Hz, its own run settings); S6 then counts only if the reference passes it

a1_definition.outcome: PASSES if every counted check PASSes; FAILS if any counted check FAILs; UNRESOLVED otherwise
a1_definition.extension: once only, if A1 or M1 is UNRESOLVED: every arm feeding an UNRESOLVED counted check (for a check made of parts, the arms feeding its UNRESOLVED parts), and M1's arm if M1 is UNRESOLVED, runs 30 more trials as <arm>_ext (seed 100 + the arm's seed); the trials are pooled, every check is scored once more on the pooled arms, and that outcome stands. No further extension; an outcome still UNRESOLVED means the decision rule does not decide, and the phase stops for review. Only if A1 FAILS is M1 not extended (the rule then says: bisect first)

criteria.ladder: reported, not scored: each rung's contralateral MN9 at sugar 100 Hz, and its difference from A1's
criteria.decision_rule: A0 fails: the reference does not reproduce here; stop. A0 passes and A1 fails: flycns differs beyond the listed settings; bisect first. A1 passes and M1 responds: the male MN9 zero is caused by flycns settings (the ladder names which). A1 passes and M1 does not respond: the male zero is wiring or annotation, not the simulator
